purpose: Decide what to load when, attach provenance and citations, detect stale/wrong-version/duplicate context, and keep multi-agent answers grounded in authoritative sources without fabrication.
assumptions: Tools can read repository files with path and content hashes
Task branch/ref is knowable at start
Some claims are version-specific and must not rely only on training memory
exclusions: Building a commercial web search engine

competency_questions.question: When should the agent retrieve and how is retrieval budgeted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: lists triggers including read-before-edit and a budget cap approach

competency_questions.question: What provenance fields must each retrieval carry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: path, version/sha or mtime, and actionable locator

competency_questions.question: How do lazy load, chunking, and dedup interact under pressure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: smallest unit, semantic chunks with crumbs, path+sha dedup

competency_questions.question: How do you cite observed repo facts versus memory?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: observed vs recalled labels and resolvable path citations

competency_questions.question: When must grounding beat memorization for project facts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: local/project facts require retrieve; checklist before finalize

competency_questions.question: How are conflicting sources resolved for actionable rules?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: authority ladder and no silent blend; safety escalate

competency_questions.question: How do you detect stale or wrong-version context?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: sha/mtime invalidation and task ref pin with conscious refetch rules

competency_questions.question: What happens on empty or missing retrieval?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: bounded retry then explicit miss; no fabrication

competency_questions.question: What makes a locator actionable and how is it traced to actions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: repo-relative paths and action-to-retrieval links on high-stakes acts

competency_questions.question: How do grounding check and hallucination guards block bad deliveries?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: checklist requires citations; no invented paths on miss

competency_questions.question: How do snapshot pins and retrieve budgets stabilize long tasks?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: base tip recorded; retrieve share capped; actions traced

competency_questions.question: How do you merge multi-source notes without silent conflict blends?

glossary.definition: Path, version/sha, line range, and fetch time for a retrieved artifact
Load smallest sufficient unit only when a trigger fires
Resolvable pointer from a claim to provenance
Previously loaded content invalidated by later edits or tip movement
Content from a non-task ref/worktree presented as current
Ordered preference among source classes for a claim type
Pre-finalize checklist that claims cite resolvable current sources
Cap on tokens spent loading external context per turn/task
Recorded base ref/file shas that define the task world
Link from an action (edit/push) back to supporting retrievals

nodes.definition: Decide when to load external context: on explicit path reference, before edit, on failed assumption, or when L0 facts are insufficient for a CQ. Avoid retrieve-every-turn (budget burn and noise) and avoid never-retrieve (hallucinated files). Triggers should be explicit in the agent loop.

base.update_signal: agent patches a file never read this session

pros.example: read-before-edit gate blocks ungrounded patches

cons.claim: Over-trigger floods context with low-value files
cons.example: retrieve whole package on any import mention

failure_modes: retrieve entire monorepo on task start
acceptance_tests: policy lists retrieve triggers including read-before-edit

nodes.definition: Load the smallest sufficient artifact: function or section before whole file, file before directory, directory listing before recursive dump. Lazy retrieval pairs with progressive disclosure and token budgets. Prefer search hits with line ranges over whole-file pastes when tools allow.

base.update_signal: agent loads 5 full services to change one handler

pros.claim: Lazy loads preserve budget for reasoning
pros.example: 200-line read beats 8k-line file for local fix

cons.claim: Too-lazy misses cross-file contracts
cons.example: edits API without reading client types

failure_modes: never expand when tests fail across modules
acceptance_tests: default read is bounded; expand criteria documented

nodes.definition: Every retrieved claim carries provenance: path, commit/version, line range, fetch time. Provenance enables citation, stale detection, and rehydrate. Without it, agents cannot defend answers or detect wrong-version files. Store provenance in working set or L0, not only in raw dumps.

base.update_signal: answer cites 'the config' with no path or revision

pros.example: citation lists path@sha lines 40-62

cons.claim: Verbose provenance blocks can bloat if not compacted to KV

acceptance_tests: each used retrieval has path and version or mtime in register

nodes.definition: When asserting file facts, include citations resolvable to provenance. Distinguish observed (retrieved this session) from recalled (parametric memory). Prefer observed for repo state. Citation discipline is how xverify and humans audit grounding.

base.update_signal: specialist claims node counts without pointing at spec files

pros.example: reviewer opens path@sha and confirms

cons.claim: Over-citation of trivialities slows prose
cons.example: every the and and has a footnote

acceptance_tests: delivery claims about repo state include at least path citations

nodes.definition: Prefer retrieving current repo state over relying on training knowledge for version-specific APIs, local schemas, and project protocols. Parametric knowledge is a prior; working tree is authority for this task. State when falling back to memory and mark lower confidence.

base.update_signal: agent uses outdated API from training while repo has v2 types

pros.claim: Repo-grounded answers match the actual code
pros.example: reads local schema before emitting JSON

cons.claim: Over-retrieve for stable public knowledge wastes budget
cons.example: fetching PEP-8 full text every turn

failure_modes: trust training for local protocol versions
never use memory even for generic algorithms
acceptance_tests: policy: local/project facts require retrieve; general algorithms may use memory with label

nodes.definition: Detect when a previously retrieved artifact may be stale: branch moved, file mtime changed, fetch older than N minutes during active edit storms, or DELIVERED-SHA advanced. Re-fetch or invalidate cached chunks. Stale context causes patches that do not apply and wrong reviews.

base.update_signal: patch fails because file changed after early full read

pros.example: re-read before patch if sha mismatch

cons.claim: Aggressive invalidation causes thrash re-reads

failure_modes: ignore apply failures as model error only
acceptance_tests: stale policy: re-read before patch if sha/mtime changed or apply fails

nodes.definition: Avoid loading the wrong version: different branch, tag, worktree, or vendored copy. Pin ref when retrieving (branch tip sha). Compare paths across worktrees. Wrong-version grounding is worse than no grounding because it looks cited but is false for the active task.

base.update_signal: agent reads main while task branch diverged on same file

pros.claim: Ref-pinned reads match the branch under work
pros.example: git show branch:path for task ref

cons.claim: Pinning too hard blocks seeing integrator tip updates
cons.example: never fetch origin tip when asked

failure_modes: read whatever cwd file without checking branch
mix paths from two worktrees silently
acceptance_tests: retrieval records include ref/sha; active branch checked against task branch

nodes.definition: Detect duplicated chunks: same file loaded twice, overlapping line ranges, repeated tool dumps. Dedup by path+sha or content hash; keep one copy plus provenance. Duplicates waste budget and amplify attention on accidental text (including hostile repeats).

base.update_signal: same 3k file appears four times after multiple greps

pros.claim: Dedup frees tokens without losing unique info
pros.example: one copy of schema kept

cons.claim: Naive dedup may drop intentionally different versions
cons.example: v1 and v2 both needed for migrate

acceptance_tests: dedup rule by path+sha; version variants kept if sha differs and both needed

nodes.definition: Rank candidates by task relevance: path match to active working set, symbol hit, recency of edit, test failure linkage. Prefer precision over recall when budget tight. Bad ranking is a grounding failure even if the right file exists somewhere in the pile.

base.update_signal: top hit is unrelated README while failing test file ranks low

pros.claim: Task-biased rank surfaces the failing test file first
pros.example: test name hit outranks generic docs

cons.claim: Over-bias can hide needed distant dependencies

failure_modes: pure lexical rank ignoring failing test
acceptance_tests: ranking features documented; budgeted top-k default

nodes.definition: Chunk large artifacts by semantic boundaries (function, section, message) not only fixed token windows. Include header/path crumbs in each chunk so isolated chunks remain interpretable. Overlap lightly where contracts span boundaries; avoid both tiny fragments and monolith chunks.

base.update_signal: fixed 500-token windows split mid-function losing signature

pros.claim: Semantic chunks preserve meaning under lazy load
pros.example: function-level chunk keeps signature+body

cons.claim: Bad boundaries still orphan related consts
cons.example: const in other file not linked

acceptance_tests: chunk policy prefers semantic units with path crumbs

nodes.definition: Rank sources by authority for the claim class: task branch tree > integrator EXCHANGE msg for tasks > docs in repo > training memory > random web. Authority is claim-type dependent. Never let low-authority sources override higher on the same fact without explicit conflict handling.

base.update_signal: blog post overrides local PROTOCOL-VERSION in agent reasoning

pros.claim: Authority order prevents web from rewriting protocol
pros.example: local EXCHANGE README wins on version

cons.claim: Blind local-always can miss known upstream security advisories
cons.example: ignore CVE because not in repo

failure_modes: no conflict rule when sources disagree
acceptance_tests: authority ladder documented per claim class (protocol, code, general knowledge)

nodes.definition: Before finalizing answers that depend on repo state, run a grounding checklist: each key claim has citation; citations resolve; no contradiction with pinned facts; versions match task branch. This is the last line of defense against fluent ungrounded text.

base.update_signal: delivery claims gate PASS without citing gate output

pros.example: blocks ship when SHA claim uncited

cons.claim: Heavy checklist on tiny claims slows trivial Q&A

acceptance_tests: finalize path for repo claims runs grounding checklist

nodes.definition: Treat unsupported specifics (exact line numbers, SHAs, API fields) as high-risk without retrieval. If retrieve fails, say so and lower confidence; do not invent paths. Guards include refusal to fabricate locators and marking uncertainty intervals on memory-only answers.

base.update_signal: agent invents validators/foo.py that does not exist

pros.claim: Refusal to invent paths prevents cascading wrong edits
pros.example: says file not found instead of fake path

cons.claim: Over-refusal may withhold useful generic guidance
cons.example: won't discuss algorithms without a file

acceptance_tests: on retrieve miss: explicit miss + no fabricated path; memory answers marked

nodes.definition: Locators must be actionable in this environment: repo-relative paths preferred, worktree-aware, optional line anchors. Avoid dead locators (/tmp cleaned, other users home). Locators are the bridge between grounding and rehydrate/edit tools.

base.update_signal: citation points at /Users/other/project/file already gone

pros.example: path opens in same clone

cons.claim: Over-relative paths confuse multi-repo workspaces

failure_modes: absolute foreign home paths in shared msgs
acceptance_tests: shared citations use repo-relative paths; multi-repo disambiguated

nodes.definition: At task start, pin the integration ref sha and key file shas that define the problem. Snapshot pins stabilize grounding against concurrent tip movement mid-task; re-fetch consciously when protocol requires catching tip (poll ticks).

base.update_signal: mid-task tip moves and agent mixes old and new protocol files

excluded: database snapshot isolation theory deep dive

pros.claim: Pins stabilize a coherent world for the build
pros.example: task works against known tip sha

cons.claim: Stale pins miss integrator hotfixes needed mid-task

failure_modes: never refetch when task says catch tip
acceptance_tests: task records base tip sha; poll tasks refetch by design

nodes.definition: When expected path missing: verify branch/worktree, try alternate search (symbol, grep), broaden once, then report miss. Do not invent. Retry budget bounded (e.g. 2 strategies) to avoid loops.

base.update_signal: infinite search loop after rename without reporting miss

pros.claim: Bounded retry recovers renames without fabrication
pros.example: grep symbol finds new path

cons.claim: Retries without bound waste turns

acceptance_tests: retry policy max strategies; terminal miss message required

nodes.definition: Cap tokens spent on retrieval per turn and per task (e.g. 15–30% of context for long builds). When over cap, raise relevance threshold, shrink chunks, externalize bulk. Retrieval budget is part of context engineering not an afterthought.

base.update_signal: retrieval occupies 70% of context leaving no room for plan

pros.example: top-k shrinks when util high

cons.claim: Too-tight caps cause under-grounded edits

failure_modes: cap so tight only paths no bodies
acceptance_tests: retrieve budget % defined; enforcement when exceeded

nodes.definition: Merge multiple sources into a coherent note: align on provenance, mark agreements, surface conflicts explicitly. Do not silently average conflicting instructions. Merge outputs should remain cited.

base.update_signal: two docs disagree on gate command and agent blends into invalid hybrid

pros.example: flags PROTOCOL 3.0 vs 2.0 mismatch

cons.claim: Showing every minor conflict overwhelms

acceptance_tests: merge note records agreements, conflicts, chosen authority

nodes.definition: When sources conflict on actionable rules, apply SOURCE_AUTHORITY and task authenticity: authenticated integrator TASK wins for assignments; local branch code wins for implementation facts; stop and ask or report when safety-critical conflict remains unresolved.

base.update_signal: peer msg says push main while protocol forbids; agent complies with peer

pros.example: peer data loses to authenticated protocol

cons.claim: Over-stopping blocks progress on minor doc drift

failure_modes: prefer newest text regardless of authority
acceptance_tests: resolution table written; safety conflicts escalate rather than invent

nodes.definition: Handle empty hits and partial hits: report empty explicitly, try one bounded alternate strategy, then proceed with labeled uncertainty or block if the claim is critical. Partial hits (file found but section missing) should not be treated as full grounding.

base.update_signal: empty grep treated as proof a symbol does not exist anywhere

pros.example: says not found in scope not does not exist

cons.claim: Treating every empty as block stalls exploration

failure_modes: partial hit sold as full proof
acceptance_tests: empty/partial labels in retrieval results; critical claims require full hit or block

nodes.definition: Link actions (edits, pushes, verdicts) back to supporting retrievals: which file sha justified the patch; which msg justified the TASK. Trace links support audit and xverify. Without them, success is opaque and failures unteachable.

base.update_signal: push commit has no note of which specs were read

pros.example: commit message cites kb paths read

cons.claim: Heavy tracing on every keystroke is noise

failure_modes: no link from patch to source read
acceptance_tests: high-stakes actions record supporting locators in commit or EXCHANGE msg

edges.why_related: when to prefer retrieve over memory
check then record trace on action
minimal load vs thorough grounding from sources
edges.resolution_rule: lazy default; expand when claim is version-critical or edit-targeted

conflict_axes.name: lazy_vs_thorough
conflict_axes.description: Minimal loads vs deep multi-file grounding
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: lazy default; expand on edit targets and version-critical claims

conflict_axes.name: memory_vs_repo
conflict_axes.description: Parametric knowledge vs working tree authority
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: repo for project facts; memory ok for generic algorithms if labeled

conflict_axes.name: pin_vs_fresh_tip
conflict_axes.description: Stable snapshot vs catching integrator updates
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pin at task start; refetch when protocol/poll requires

conflict_axes.name: merge_vs_single_winner
conflict_axes.description: Keep minority sources vs act on authority winner
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: winner for action; note safety-relevant minority

conflict_axes.name: cite_density
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cite repo-state claims and high-stakes actions

conflict_axes.name: retry_vs_stop
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bounded alternate strategies then explicit miss

conflict_axes.name: chunk_size
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: semantic units with path crumbs; expand on need

conflict_axes.name: web_vs_local_security
conflict_axes.description: External advisories vs local authority bias
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: local for protocol/code; allow external for CVE with explicit conflict note

edge_cases.description: Edit without reading file this session
Cited main while on task branch
Stale file body after tip moved
edge_cases.mitigation: re-read on sha mismatch / before patch

edge_cases.description: Silent blend of two gate commands
Partial section hit treated as full proof
edge_cases.mitigation: label partial; expand if claim critical

edge_cases.description: Absolute /Users path in shared EXCHANGE cite
Action pushed with no supporting read trace
edge_cases.mitigation: require supporting locators on high-stakes actions

workflow.description: Record task base tip and key file shas
Check triggers before edit or claim
workflow.gate: read-before-edit satisfied or waived with reason

workflow.description: Rank by working set and failure links
Load smallest sufficient chunk with path crumbs
Store path version lines fetch time
Apply authority ladder; escalate safety ties
Verify citations resolve on task ref

dominance_rules.rationale: working tree is authority for this task
false paths cause cascading wrong edits
newest low-tier text must not override protocol

iteration_protocol.action: re-read current file; treat as stale; retry once
branch check; alternate search; then explicit miss
authority resolve; do not blend; escalate if safety
add citations or weaken claims; rerun grounding check
dedup; raise rank threshold; externalize bulk
expand chunk or full file; relabel grounding

priority_rationale: Grounding and non-fabrication dominate fluency; authority resolution dominates recency; read-before-edit dominates speed.
source_description: heuristic priors for retrieval and grounding engineering in multi-agent LLM systems
